title: Science Salon
subtitle: On understanding each individual at Laplace.

trails.title: Scholarly Exchange
trails.description: Exchange is one thing, and competition is another. Without both, how can we improve?

content.text: Be ever so careful, dear. The fiery thirst for knowledge is blazing bright within you; be careful not to put it out.
Once, many fire thieves sat here, sipping coffee, as they tried to decipher the best angle to hold up their reeds to jam the burning wheel of Helios and steal his flame.
The gods are selfish. They're stingy with their might.
Shouldn't the gods be more generous?

branch.text: That's easy to say when the power's not yours to give. Knowing how to share is a rare virtue. Knowing how to share knowledge is a rarer virtue still.
"How can we transfer our wisdom into mortal minds?" The gods pondered.
Can inspiration be duplicated from one brain to another? It comes and goes like a gust of wind, so what can be done?
True. I'm sure the early customers of the bakery share the same philosophy.
The line must be respected, however hungry the latecomers may be.
There are many fire thieves in the field of science—many more than the bread buyers in the bakery. Take a look at these geeks in uniforms made of aerospace materials.
Among them are arcanists in love with science who spend most of their time studying diodes and machines, and humans who are passionate about the future, always finding new inspirations ...
Elements, lightning, atoms ... Perhaps you've forgotten their counterparts in arcanum, but you must be familiar with them as scientific discoveries.

These discoveries are the milestones of progress, sweetheart. The fire thieves firmly believed that they would be able to bring about many more technical revolutions: the fourth, the fifth, the 65535th ...
Sounds like a twist to the story is coming.
Not yet, darling. We've only finished the prologue. However, there is a "but" waiting down the road.
A sudden rain dampened people's enthusiasm for the future. The floppy disks and many clever minds perished in it.
Some of the fire thieves grieved the loss. They screamed and swore to retrieve what was lost.
What about the rest of them?
They returned to primitive chaos, like coelacanths crawling back into the ocean after thousands of years of evolution. Once again, they became the proteges of arcanum.
Perhaps they made the right choice by leaving that useless science behind. Who knows?
The story of the fire thieves has only gone this far, darling. At this point, no one knows what will happen to Prometheus or what's inside Pandora's box.

content.text: Some will receive it. First come, first served.

items.text: An unofficial meeting on the "Artificial Storm" project was held before the "Free Breeze" set sail from Australia.

items.speaker: Attendee I
items.text: Did you wake up with a glitch this morning, Ulrich?

items.speaker: Attendee I
items.text: The "Storm" has already taken so many lives, and now you're planning to intentionally bring another one upon us?!
Laplace Conference Hall

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Quit your worrying, Jonathan. The "Artificial Storm" will be under strict control, and you're not even on the research team.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Besides, there are some issues we still need to fix, so we've come to a bit of a standstill for now.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I promise, you won't wake up to find the building engulfed by the "Storm."

items.speaker: Attendee I
items.text: Sorry, are you saying that you've already started?!

items.speaker: Attendee II
items.text: Ulrich, I have to warn you.

items.speaker: Attendee II
items.text: Ever since you found that satellite, you've been pushing past the limits of Laplace's regulations.

items.speaker: Attendee II
items.text: You've accessed materials from other branches, used valuable resources for your own purposes, and run experiments without proper clearance.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: What baseless claims, Penelope! I'll have you know that everything I've done has been approved by the HQ director.

items.speaker: Attendee I
items.text: Director? We don't have a damn director!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: But we do have a "substitute director." So there.
He gives a pointed nod in Enigma's direction.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: For the last time, I'm not the "substitute director." No one can substitute for Madam Lucy.
That familiar heavy knock on the table resounds once more.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But let's set that aside. We're here to figure out what to do with the satellite, not to stage an intervention for Ulrich.

items.speaker: Attendee III
items.text: The solution's as clear as day, my friends!

items.speaker: Attendee III
items.text: We'll do exactly what they did in Plesetsk during the third "Storm." Find someone brave and send them into space!

items.speaker: Attendee IV
items.text: He's right. Why don't we just build another satellite and see how it handles the "Storm"?
A sarcastic applause suddenly erupts.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Wow, what an amazing idea! Truly a stroke of genius! So, we're talking about a controlled experiment, right?

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: That means we'll send not just one, but dozens of satellites, all carrying different items!

items.speaker: Attendee IV
items.text: What's the problem with that?

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Oh, nothing. The budget team will be thrilled at the idea. Here's a better one: We sit tight and wait till the "Storm" sends us back to 1995.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: And bingo! Surprise!! There's our satellite, orbiting around the Earth once again.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Medicine Pocket, please mind your tone in the meeting room.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Oh sure, just as soon as they stop trying to waste all our research funds.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I'm with Researcher Medicine Pocket here.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: There's no need to launch more satellites. We should be focusing on the "Artificial Storm" project.
Ulrich knocks the table, drawing everyone's attention.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: The project has made substantial progress!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I have collected every item that was once on the "Regulus Satellite," including the space seeds from Plesetsk. You have no idea how difficult that was; let me tell you! It was easier to get Regulus's record!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Still, you probably didn't need to steal it, Ulrich!

items.speaker: Attendee V
items.text: You say that, but I've heard that it isn't going all that smoothly!

items.speaker: Attendee V
items.text: Accelerating the reaction of asymmetrical nuclide R with fixed-frequency sound waves so as to simulate the "Storm." It sounds impressive, but ...

items.speaker: Attendee V
items.text: What's the payoff? Have you found the key material that provides immunity from the "Storm"?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Good point, Lukas. I never claimed the experiment was perfect. In fact, I'll be the first to admit that it has some serious procedural flaws.

items.speaker: Attendee V
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Through 26 microscale "Artificial Storms," I tested seven different space seeds, an astronomical spectrometer, a high-speed photometer, some obsidian crystals, and a Lycopus lucidus talisman.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: None of them endured the trials.

items.speaker: Attendee V
items.text: So, what do we do now? Just give up?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: No!
Ulrich awkwardly clears his throat.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: But I have used all the asymmetrical nuclide R that we had in the warehouse.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: What?!
Medicine Pocket springs to their feet like a shocked animal.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Sit down, Medicine Pocket! Jonathan, go get them a stress ball!

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: No! I can shout all I want, okay, "substitute director"?!
Medicine Pocket slams the table, sending papers flying.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Ulrich! All the asymmetrical nuclide R? It's all gone?!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I had to use it. It's just standard consumption, like in any other experiment! And I got results!

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: With that amount of resources, of course you'd find something, dumbass! Even a broken clock's right twice a day!

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Keep at it if you want. You're gonna smash that dead end head-on!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I don't see why you're commenting on my work. We're not even in the same department.
Ulrich presses down on the table to ease the vibrations shaking the ferrofluid in his tank.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Because you used my materials! That was most of the nuclide R from both Laplace and the Foundation!

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: You have to be kidding me! You get all you want while I'm here, like some chump, filling out endless forms just to get a few drops!
The badge on Medicine Pocket's chest creaks under the stress of their shouts.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Next time, just give me the funds and nuclide, and I'll be more than happy to run a few laps in the "Storm" with that crap from the satellite and see what happens!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We would never endanger the life of a researcher like that.

items.speaker: Attendee III
items.text: That's why we should launch another satellite! No need to risk anyone's life, especially since we've got plenty of colleagues with aeronautics experience.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Can't do that. Our best space expert is still in the Laplace care unit.
The smoke temporarily clears, and finally, one member returns the meeting to its main agenda.

items.speaker: Attendee II
items.text: So, Ulrich, what's the next step with your experiment?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I'm taking it outside, of course.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: The richest deposits of asymmetrical nuclide R aren't in the lab or the Foundation's warehouse. They're out there in the real world!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We've been overlooking how the density of nuclide R has affected our experiment results.

items.speaker: Attendee V
items.text: Come on, Ulrich, that's just an excuse. Where would you find a higher nuclide R density than in a Laplace lab?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: That might be the exact problem. The environment here is too controlled, too clean. The "Storm" has never been the manifestation of order, but of chaos.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And how exactly do you plan on finding chaos?
The scientists are fighting tooth and nail to secure the budgets for their individual projects.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Everyone, please!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: If we just sit here arguing instead of getting out there and doing something, those sneaky researchers at Institutum Lorentz are going to get ahead of us!
He slams a butterfly-patterned envelope heavily onto the table, adding yet more fuel to the fiery chaos.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Lorentz. That strange secret society?

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Let's see what kind of bull they're spouting this time!

items.speaker: Attendee II
items.text: No, Medicine Pocket! Just toss the letter into the shredder!
Hurried footsteps echo, and a clear voice cuts through the chaos.

items.speaker: Simone
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen, my apologies for interrupting your debate. The St. Pavlov Foundation has passed a new resolution.
